claim: HASS.Agent is a Windows-only .NET 8 Home Assistant companion client and explicitly states it is not a Linux/macOS client, with cross-platform support only a hopeful wish for a future v3 rewrite
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must stand on its own as the Linux-side agent; no convergence with HASS.Agent is coming
scope_conditions: HASS.Agent platform, as of 2.2.1 (Jun 2025); Windows only
quoted_support: What it's not — A Linux/macOS client (at least yet)! ... We are thinking about cross-platform support for the "v3 rewrite" but as of now it's only a hopeful wish. You can try the official companion app for macOS, or IoPC which runs on Linux.

claim: HASS.Agent's Satellite Service collects sensor data and executes commands even when no user is logged in, establishing headless operation as a shipped companion-agent pattern
stance_target: ha-linux-agent fleet-wide design should treat headless/no-login collection as a first-class requirement, not a kiosk special case
scope_conditions: Windows service architecture; not all commands/sensors available to the Satellite Service
quoted_support: Satellite Service: use the service to collect sensor data and execute commands, even when you're not logged in (not all commands/sensors are available for Satellite Service)

claim: HASS.Agent auto-registers all commands and sensors into Home Assistant via the MQTT integration, with a separate HA-side integration required for notifications and media player
stance_target: MQTT discovery is the established bidirectional channel for companion agents; ha-linux-agent's MQTT-centric approach matches the incumbent architecture
quoted_support: Commands and sensors are automatically added to your Home Assistant instance via MQTT Integration. ... This requires the installation of the HASS.Agent integration. (for notifications and media player)

claim: HASS.Agent 2.2.0 removed the LibreHardwareMonitor library (WinRing0 kernel-driver security issue) and as a result the GPU Temperature Sensor is permanently non-functioning (always returns 0)
stance_target: privileged hardware-sensor access is a long-term security liability; a fleet agent should avoid kernel-driver-dependent hardware sensing
quoted_support: Due to security concerns, we were forced to remove Libre Hardware Monitor library that allowed HASS.Agent to access hardware information. The breaking change in this is that starting with this release, the GPU Temperature Sensor is non-functioning. It has been left present for backward compatibility reasons, however it will always return 0.

claim: HASS.Agent's release history documents recurring MQTT-discovery and sensor-pipeline reliability failures of exactly the class a fleet-wide Linux agent must defend against: autodiscovery messages not republished after broker reconnect (#230), MQTT entity IDs changing on device rename (#388), discovery messages not removed on rename (#376), and all WMI sensors stopping when the WMI service restarts (#205)
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's 'never reliable' complaint is a known hard problem class across companion agents; re-publish-on-reconnect and stable entity identity are the specific mechanisms to get right
quoted_support: MQTT autodiscovery messages were not republished after connection was lost and recovered (thanks to @whc2001 for reporting) #230 ... Fixed MQTT entities changing ID after device rename #388 ... Restarting "Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI)" while HASS.Agent is running causes all WMI based sensors to stop functioning #205

claim: HASS.Agent 2.2.0 added the ability to test the MQTT connection during onboarding and an experimental WebSocket option for MQTT connections
stance_target: onboarding-time MQTT validation and transport selection are table-stakes UX for a fleet agent's first-run experience
quoted_support: Added ability to test MQTT connection during onboarding process (thanks to @jgstew for suggestion) #379 ... Added WebSocket support for MQTT connections (experimental :)) #253
